title: Stateful session replay trace workload + memory-pressure reporting pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: synthetic workload generators do not exercise stateful cache eviction patterns or the site-specific session characteristics we observe in production. This PR introduces a stateful session-replay trace workload that replays sampled production traces (anonymized) into the inference runtime to surface memory growth, KV cache churn, and tail-latency amplification tied to long-prefix sequences. It also adds a memory-pressure reporting pipeline that emits continuous flamegraph-ready samples, eviction histograms, and sequence-length correlated tail-latency reports. The description below covers what changed, how to run it, and expected outputs. What changed: 1) new trace-replayer service (benchmark-lab/replayers/session_replay.py) that replays per-session request sequences preserving timing and KV-cache warm state semantics; 2) a synthetic-trace normalizer (benchmark-lab/tools/trace_normalizer.go) to turn raw event logs into compact replay traces; 3) memory-pressure reporter (benchmark-lab/reporters/memory_reporter/README.md + reporter binary) that samples process RSS, allocator histograms, and generates folded stack traces for flamegraph ingestion; 4) CI harness additions that run a lightweight replay against the canary runtime in CI and verify no regression in peak memory per-session; 5) dashboards and exporter glue (grafana/board/session-replay-memory.json and exporters/prom/memory_replay_exporter.yaml) to visualize eviction counters vs tail latency. How to run locally: use ./tools/trace_normalizer to convert a trace, then ./replayers/session_replay --trace ./out/normalized_trace.json --concurrency 12 --preserve-interval-ms 50 --warmup 120s --target-url http://localhost:8080; memory reporter can be run with ./reporters/memory_reporter --pid-file ./pidfile --output ./reports/session_$(date +%Y%m%d).folded --sample-interval 250ms. Outputs: folded flamegraph files, eviction histograms (buckets: 0-10,10-50,50-200,200+ evictions/session), per-session peak-RSS timeseries, and a CSV correlating sequence_length, peak_rss, and P99 latency. Compatibility & safety: replayer respects rate limits and has a dry-run mode; normalized traces automatically scrub PII and user IDs; memory reporter requires root on some platforms for frame unwinding. Caveats: the reporter's symbolization step can be slow on stripped binaries; CI runs use a pared-down configuration to avoid slow symbolization. This PR is focused on observability and benchmark fidelity — it does not change runtime-serving code paths.

diff_snippet:
--- a/benchmark-lab/replayers/session_replay.py
+++ b/benchmark-lab/replayers/session_replay.py
@@ def replay_session(session):
-    for req in session.requests:
-        send(req)
+    # preserve kv-cache warm semantics: replay prefix before measuring tail
+    prefix, tail = session.split_prefix_tail(prefix_len=30)
+    for r in prefix:
+        send(r, record_kv_warm=True)
+    sleep(session.inter_request_ms / 1000.0)
+    for r in tail:
+        send(r)
review_conversation: Diego Alvarez: Nice. Two questions: 1) do benchmarks require symbolized binaries in CI? 2) could the normalizer accidentally drop important timing jitter that affects cache behavior?

Maya Chen (author): CI uses a stripped run by default, symbolization is off in the CI smoke test to keep runtime fast; full symbolization is supported in nightly. The normalizer preserves inter-event deltas exactly unless --collapse-idle is set; added tests to assert time deltas are preserved (test_trace_normalizer_time_preservation).
Priya Kapoor: Can we add an opt-in flag so enterprise customers don't upload traces to our CI? Also add a note about trace retention policy in the README.
Maya Chen: added --no-upload flag and updated README with retention guidance; SUP-1221 linked for the privacy checklist.
Nikhil Rao: CI flake: allocator histogram sample on linux-arm hangs sometimes. Added a retry wrapper around the sample call. Verified in the third CI run. Approving now.
testing_summary: Local run: 12 concurrency, 1k sessions, peak memory observed 820MB (baseline 610MB) for long-tail sessions: analysis artifacts attached.
CI run: smoke replay with 50 sessions, validated peak_rss < 1.2x baseline, reported as pass.
Nightly: scheduled full replay against canary with symbolization enabled (handled outside this PR).
perf_results_summary: Initial runs show a reproducible increase in per-session peak RSS when long-prefix sequences are present; eviction histogram identifies small-but-frequent KV churn as main contributor. The reporter produces folded stacks that point to allocator hotspots in the runtime sharding layer. Recommendations: follow-up PR to add small heap-slab tuning and a KV compacting path if regression persists.
release_notes: Added a stateful session-replay workload and a memory-pressure reporting pipeline to benchmark-lab. New tools: trace_normalizer, session_replay, memory_reporter. New dashboards and CI smoke tests to track eviction patterns and per-session memory regressions.
